# Behavioral Specification: OTP Key Derivation Interface

## 1. Overview

The OTP key derivation interface provides key-derivation and token-hashing services for other hardware requesters. It accepts requests for:

- hashing a life-cycle unlock token,
- deriving static flash scrambling keys,
- deriving ephemeral SRAM and OTBN scrambling keys and nonces.

The module uses a shared scrambling/digest datapath and an entropy source to produce the requested outputs. It shall arbitrate among multiple simultaneous requesters and process one request at a time.

## 2. Reset and Initialization

After reset, the module shall be in a safe inactive state:

- No request shall be acknowledged.
- All key, token, nonce, and seed-valid outputs shall be reset to their inactive/default values.
- No entropy requests shall be issued.
- No scrambling resource requests shall be issued.

The module shall remain inactive until an enable indication is asserted. Requests received before enable shall be ignored.

Once the enable indication is asserted, the module shall enter the idle state and begin accepting requests. The enable indication only needs to be sampled after reset; deasserting it later shall not stop an in-progress operation.

## 3. Request Arbitration

When idle, the module shall accept requests from the following request classes:

- life-cycle token hashing,
- flash data key derivation,
- flash address key derivation,
- OTBN key derivation,
- SRAM key derivation slots.

If multiple requests are pending at the same time, the module shall arbitrate fairly so that no request source is permanently starved. Only one request shall be processed at a time. The other requests shall remain pending and be serviced later.

The request source shall keep its request and all associated data stable until the corresponding acknowledge is asserted. The module relies on this behavior to guarantee correct derivation.

## 4. Request Completion and Outputs

When the module finishes processing a request, it shall:

1. Make all data outputs for that request stable.
2. Assert the corresponding acknowledge output.
3. Keep the outputs stable after acknowledge until a later request replaces them.

Data outputs are meaningful only while the matching acknowledge is asserted; at other times they may contain values from a previous request.

## 5. Request Types

### 5.1 Life-Cycle Token Hashing

For a life-cycle token hash request:

- The module shall accept a 128-bit token input.
- No entropy shall be mixed into the hashing operation.
- The module shall produce a 128-bit hashed token.
- The two 64-bit halves of the hashed token shall be generated in a chained fashion so that the second half depends on the first half.
- An acknowledge shall be asserted only after the hashed token is available.

### 5.2 Flash Data and Address Key Derivation

For flash key derivation requests:

- The module shall accept a 256-bit key seed.
- No entropy shall be mixed into the derivation.
- The module shall produce a 128-bit key.
- Each 64-bit half of the output key shall be derived independently from the corresponding 128-bit half of the 256-bit seed.
- Flash data key requests and flash address key requests shall use distinct derivation configurations.
- A seed-valid output shall accompany the key, indicating whether the key seed was valid.
- An acknowledge shall be asserted only after the key and seed-valid output are stable.

### 5.3 SRAM Key Derivation

For each SRAM key request:

- The module shall use the SRAM data key seed plus fresh entropy.
- The module shall produce a 128-bit derivation key.
- Each 64-bit half of the derivation key shall be produced independently using the seed and fresh entropy.
- The module shall also produce a nonce output consisting of one fresh 64-bit entropy word.
- A seed-valid output shall accompany the key, indicating whether the key seed was valid.
- An acknowledge shall be asserted only after the key, nonce, and seed-valid output are stable.

### 5.4 OTBN Key Derivation

For an OTBN key request:

- The module shall use the SRAM data key seed plus fresh entropy.
- The module shall produce a 128-bit derivation key.
- Each 64-bit half of the derivation key shall be produced independently using the seed and fresh entropy.
- The module shall also produce a nonce output consisting of two fresh 64-bit entropy words.
- A seed-valid output shall accompany the key, indicating whether the key seed was valid.
- An acknowledge shall be asserted only after the key, nonce, and seed-valid output are stable.

## 6. Entropy Acquisition

The module shall request entropy only for SRAM and OTBN key derivation requests. Flash key derivation and life-cycle token hashing shall not request entropy.

For requests that require entropy:

- The module shall assert an entropy request and wait until the entropy source acknowledges.
- The module shall not proceed without the required entropy.
- The entropy words used in the key derivation shall be fresh words supplied by the entropy source.
- The nonce output shall consist of raw entropy words, not words passed through the digest operation.
- If a key seed is invalid, the module shall still request entropy and perform the derivation using zero for the seed.

## 7. Scrambling Resource Usage

Before performing any key derivation or token hash, the module shall request exclusive access to the shared scrambling/digest datapath and wait until access is granted.

While processing a request, the module shall:

- initialize the digest as required for the request type,
- feed the required data blocks,
- finalize the digest computation,
- wait for the result,
- capture the resulting output data.

The module shall hold the scrambling resource until all digest work for the current request is complete. It shall release the resource before performing a nonce-only fetch, since nonce fetch does not require the scrambling datapath.

## 8. Seed Validity

The module receives a seed-valid indication for the key derivation seeds.

- If the seed-valid indication is asserted, the module shall use the provided seed values and return seed-valid asserted.
- If the seed-valid indication is deasserted, the module shall substitute all-zero data for the key seed, still perform the derivation, and return seed-valid deasserted.
- Life-cycle token hashing shall always treat the token as valid and does not return a seed-valid output.

The seed-valid output shall be stable before the corresponding acknowledge is asserted.

## 9. Error and Escalation Behavior

The module shall support an escalation indication. When escalation is active, the module shall move to a terminal error state regardless of whether a request is currently being processed.

In the terminal error state, the module shall:

- stop processing all requests,
- not acknowledge any pending request,
- not issue any new entropy requests,
- not issue any new scrambling resource requests,
- withdraw any outstanding resource or entropy requests,
- assert the error status output continuously,
- not update key, token, nonce, or seed-valid outputs,
- remain in the terminal error state until reset.

If the internal control logic reaches an illegal or unrecognized state, the module shall also enter the terminal error state and assert the error status output.

If an error occurs while a request is in progress, that request shall not receive an acknowledge.

## 10. Output Stability

After a request completes and its acknowledge is asserted, the data outputs for that request shall remain stable until the module begins producing outputs for a subsequent accepted request. At minimum, the outputs are guaranteed to remain stable while the module is idle or waiting for a new request.

The module shall not change the data outputs for a completed request before asserting the acknowledge.
